Independent senators are a threat to our parliamentary system
Let the Lieutenant-Governors appoint their own Senators. (at the recommendation of the voters of the Province if that province wants elected senators).

The idea of democratically elected Senators is one that is not without merit - depending of course on how they are elected. In case you're wondering, I do not consider FPTP as the pinnacle of democracy given that the winner is usually elected by the greatest minority instead of any sort of majority.

That said, elected Senators would suffer from the same failings that elected MPs suffer from. The way our party system has developed they are responsible first and foremost to the party and the will of its leader, and unless an individual MP is willing to suffer expulsion from the party, lose his/her office, budget, and party perks, and find themselves sitting in a dark corner at the back of the room, their constituents come a distant second. Principles and strong spines are few and far between on the back benches, most MPs are content to read the lines handed to them as they walk into The House and to vote how and when the Party whip tells them to - what leads you to believe that the Senate would be any different, or any better, for that?

what leads you to believe that the Senate would be any different, or any better, for that?

Nothing. I support appointed senators. But if some Lieutenant-Governor wants to appoint the same guy that his province voted-for, then by all means do so.

The more interesting (and unique) part of my proposal is the one you didn't respond to at all: letting each Province's L.G. do the appointing instead of the Commons' Prime Minister.

The L.G.'s of each province suffer from the same failings as G.G's do, they are political appointees with ceremonial roles who do what they are told. It would, however, introduce an element of more localness to the process with Premiers deciding who would represent the province/territory.
